Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0014", "row_sha256": "2f5d987c23c9d48e65a9bd3c2454e9cff347f74374f9d45f8cea00ddd853d7f3", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "um i checked the ventilation in the north workshop this morning before the metal class started the exhaust fan above the soldering benches was running but it sounded rough and the airflow at the left hood felt weaker than it did last week i asked mara to hold a strip of tissue near each opening while i watched the indicator on the wall panel she asked whether the weak pull was only at the left hood and i said uh-huh before showing her the readings the two center hoods pulled the tissue inward steadily and the left one barely moved it the filter gauge is still in the green but close to the lower mark and there was a little dust along the frame well the door to the storage bay was propped open during the check so that may have changed the reading i closed it and waited about three minutes before checking again the left hood was still weak i wrote the time and readings on the paper log and took a photo of the gauge i haven't opened the fan casing or adjusted anything because i don't know whether facilities wants us to leave it untouched until they inspect it could you send them the photo and ask when someone can come by before the next soldering session", "output": "I checked the ventilation in the north workshop this morning before the metal class started. The exhaust fan above the soldering benches was running, but it sounded rough, and the airflow at the left hood felt weaker than it did last week. I asked Mara to hold a strip of tissue near each opening while I watched the indicator on the wall panel. She asked whether the weak pull was only at the left hood, and I said uh-huh before showing her the readings. The two center hoods pulled the tissue inward steadily, and the left one barely moved it. The filter gauge is still in the green but close to the lower mark, and there was a little dust along the frame. Well, the door to the storage bay was propped open during the check, so that may have changed the reading. I closed it and waited about three minutes before checking again. The left hood was still weak. I wrote the time and readings on the paper log and took a photo of the gauge. I haven't opened the fan casing or adjusted anything because I don't know whether facilities wants us to leave it untouched until they inspect it. Could you send them the photo and ask when someone can come by before the next soldering session?"}]
